macros.name: DerNorm
macros.doc: The commands “\DerTot{. . . }{. . . }”, “\DerPar{. . . }{. . . }” and “\DerNorm{. . . }” generate the symbols of total derivative, partial derivative and normal derivative, respectively.

macros.name: DerPar
macros.doc: The commands “\DerTot{. . . }{. . . }”, “\DerPar{. . . }{. . . }” and “\DerNorm{. . . }” generate the symbols of total derivative, partial derivative and normal derivative, respectively.

macros.name: DerTot
macros.doc: The commands “\DerTot{. . . }{. . . }”, “\DerPar{. . . }{. . . }” and “\DerNorm{. . . }” generate the symbols of total derivative, partial derivative and normal derivative, respectively.

macros.name: Div
macros.doc: The \Grad, \Div and \Rot commands generates a symbol or a roman word, depending on the selected option.

macros.name: Grad
macros.doc: The \Grad, \Div and \Rot commands generates a symbol or a roman word, depending on the selected option.

macros.name: Int
macros.doc: The “\Int” (capitalized) differs from the LaTeX command “\int” in that it is always printed in displaystyle and if it has only a subscript, this is somewhat lowered so that it looks better.

macros.name: ProdVett
macros.doc: The command “\ProdVett” is intended for making the symbol of vector product, and evaluates to “\times” with the option “ProdVettTimes” and to “\wedge” with the (default) option “ProdVettWedge”.

macros.name: Rot
macros.doc: The \Grad, \Div and \Rot commands generates a symbol or a roman word, depending on the selected option.

macros.name: TendsTo
macros.doc: The command “\TendsTo[· · · , · · ·]” generates a right-arrow with optionally an underscript wich is another smaller right-arrow between the two comma-separeted arguments inside the square brackets.

macros.name: text
macros.doc: The “\text{. . . }” command is defined to be equivalent to “\mbox” (except when the “amstext” package is also used, since this package already defines this command in a better way).

macros.name: UnderDot
macros.doc: The original work of “\d” (i.e. place a dot under its argument) is now done by the “\UnderDot” command.
